tr.td: Persistent yearning for his wife, broken sleep, low mood and withdrawal from friends and work, a year after her death; cause under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his wife's documented death a year before; resolved into the diagnosis of prolonged grief disorder at the consultation. Not a claim about his real grief.
Tobacco use disorder, cigars: about fifteen cigars a day, smoking since boyhood, some smoke inhaled; first cigar within thirty minutes of waking
S — Synthetic modern coding anchored to his documented smoking since boyhood.
Chest tightness on climbing steep hills, twice in the past month, easing within five minutes of rest; none at rest; cause under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting symptom; resolved into a diagnosis at five weeks after CT coronary angiography. Not a claim about his real heart in 1905; his documented chest pain began in 1909.

list.item: Persistent yearning for his wife, broken sleep, low mood and withdrawal from friends and work, a year after her death; cause under evaluation: active, confirmed [S]
Tobacco use disorder, cigars: about fifteen cigars a day, smoking since boyhood, some smoke inhaled; first cigar within thirty minutes of waking: active, confirmed [S]
Chest tightness on climbing steep hills, twice in the past month, easing within five minutes of rest; none at rest; cause under evaluation: active, confirmed [S]
Gout, recurrent flares of the big toe since his late fifties, two in the past year; serum urate 8.6 mg/dL; no tophi: active, confirmed [S]

Geriatric psychiatry consultation to confirm the diagnosis, separate prolonged grief disorder from major depression, advise on grief therapy, medicine and sleep, and review suicide risk. Guideline: Prolonged Grief Disorder (DSM-5-TR criteria, patient and family information) (2022); Validation of the new DSM-5-TR criteria for prolonged grief disorder and the PG-13-Revised (PG-13-R) scale (2021); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024) [S]

Safety: a structured safety assessment, a written safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in his phone, means safety, a telephone call in three days, and safety review at every visit. Guideline: Loss of partner and suicide risks among oldest old: a population-based register study (2004); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, ischemic heart disease, hyperlipidemia, and depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monographs (2026) [S]

Tobacco: his readiness asked at every visit; brief advice linked to his own concern about his heart; counseling at each visit and the state quitline; varenicline offered as the most effective single medicine, with combination nicotine replacement as the alternative. Guideline: Tobacco Smoking Cessation in Adults, Including Pregnant Persons: Interventions (2021) [S]

Chest tightness on exertion: resting ECG today and CT coronary angiography, chosen over stress testing for a man over 65 with stable symptoms and no known coronary disease; call 911 for chest pain at rest or lasting more than fifteen minutes. Guideline: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain (2021) [S]

Social connection and his writing: one planned social contact a week, a return to morning writing on a set project, and the clinic social worker's list of local groups; meaning and goals to be part of any grief treatment. Guideline: Treatment of complicated grief: a randomized controlled trial (2005) [S]

Gout: urate measured at intake; urate-lowering therapy explained, since two flares in a year make it strongly recommended; he chose to decide after the chest evaluation; call at the first sign of a flare. Guideline: 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout (2020) [S]

Cardiovascular risk: blood pressure at each visit and lipids, hemoglobin A1c and kidney function at baseline; prediabetes (hemoglobin A1c 5.8 percent) managed with walking and diet. Guideline: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain (2021); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, ischemic heart disease, hyperlipidemia, and depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monographs (2026) [S]
